profile.headline: The only hantavirus with firmly documented person-to-person transmission.
profile.syndrome: Hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome as for Sin Nombre virus, with case fatality 25–40%.
profile.transmission: Rodent excreta, and — uniquely — person-to-person spread documented in Argentine and Chilean clusters including a 2018–2019 outbreak traced through close contacts.
profile.geography: Argentina, Chile, and related viruses across South America.
profile.management: Supportive with ECMO; contact tracing and isolation are warranted, unlike for other hantaviruses.
profile.prevention: Rodent control plus respiratory and contact precautions for cases.
evidence: Epidemiological and genomic evidence of interhuman chains, including the El Bolsón 1996 and Epuyén 2018 outbreaks.

profile.headline: Cause of nephropathia epidemica, the mild form of HFRS and the most common hantavirus disease in Europe.
profile.syndrome: Fever, severe headache, abdominal and back pain, transient myopia, proteinuria and acute kidney injury; thrombocytopenia is typical. Case fatality below 0.5%, but hospitalisation is often required.
profile.transmission: Inhalation of aerosolised excreta of bank voles; incidence tracks vole population cycles and mast years.
profile.geography: Fennoscandia, the Baltic states, central and western Europe, Russia.
profile.diagnosis: IgM/IgG serology (rapid tests available); RT-PCR early.
profile.prevention: Rodent exclusion from dwellings; precautions when cleaning sheds and cabins. No vaccine in Europe.
evidence: Thousands of serologically confirmed cases annually in Finland and Sweden alone.

geo.text: Fennoscandia, the Baltic states, central and western Europe, Russia.

profile.headline: Cause of hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome in North America, identified during the 1993 Four Corners outbreak.
profile.syndrome: A short prodrome of fever and myalgia, then abrupt non-cardiogenic pulmonary oedema and cardiogenic shock; case fatality ~35–40%. Renal involvement is minimal, in contrast to HFRS.
profile.transmission: Inhalation of aerosolised excreta of deer mice, often in enclosed rural buildings.
profile.geography: Western and central United States, Canada, Mexico.
profile.diagnosis: IgM/IgG serology, RT-PCR; immunoblast-rich peripheral smear and haemoconcentration are early clues.
profile.management: Early transfer to a centre with ECMO capability is the key intervention; cautious fluid management.
profile.prevention: Rodent-proofing and safe cleaning practice (wet methods, no sweeping). No vaccine.
evidence: 1993 outbreak investigation established the virus, reservoir and syndrome within months; continuous confirmed surveillance since.

geo.text: Western and central United States, Canada, Mexico.

profile.headline: Prototype hantavirus and cause of the severe form of haemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) in East Asia.
profile.syndrome: Five classical phases — febrile, hypotensive, oliguric, diuretic and convalescent — with haemorrhage, acute kidney injury and shock; case fatality 5–15%.
profile.transmission: Inhalation of aerosolised excreta of infected rodents; no arthropod vector and essentially no person-to-person spread (except Andes virus).
profile.management: Supportive with careful fluid balance and renal replacement therapy; early ribavirin has shown benefit in HFRS.
profile.prevention: Rodent control, dust-avoidance precautions; inactivated vaccines (Hantavax) used in Korea and China.
evidence: Identified in 1976 from Apodemus lung tissue after the Korean War epidemic of ~3000 UN troops; abundant confirmed clinical data since.
